 How far could Nvidia's stock fall on Huang's resignation? What investors need to know
 Published Wed, Nov 11 2026 7:43 PM EST Updated 4 Hours Ago Tobias Burns WATCH LIVE Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday following revelations that he had an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies allege is a Chinese spy. The shares were down 12% on Thursday. Analysts said they could fall even further. "When you have a founder-led company, and there's no clear number two, that is a recipe for a 20% correction," Gene Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, said before the Huang resignation news broke. Jay Goldberg at Seaport Research Partners also said that the stock could see a 20% hit following a sudden departure of Huang, but he suggested it could fall a lot more due to the CEO's managerial centrality at the company. "If he gets fired tomorrow, or whatever happens to him tomorrow, the stock is down 20%," he said on Wednesday. "But that's just the near-term impact – the shock value. He's built this company. He founded it. He's grown it to where it is. He's the only CEO the company's ever had, and he structured the company in such a way [that] he is at the center of everything. He has 70 direct reports." NVDA 1D mountain Nvidia, 1 day Huang issued an apology on Sunday after The New York Times reported that he had an extramarital relationship with a woman intelligence agencies identified as a spy . On Wednesday afternoon, The New York Times reported that Huang is also said to have had a relationship with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him. Minutes after that news broke, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove Huang . Thursday morning before the bell, Huang was out. Huang's scandal wouldn't be the first time that a company's stock took a hit as a result of reported marital affairs or espionage claims involving a CEO. Many different companies have come under pressure on similar news, according to research from Mizuho. However, these historic examples may not apply here because of how interconnected Huang was with the company's daily operations, with many more direct reports above the norm. He also was considered the leading figure in the AI boom, orchestrating financial deals for the whole industry. Despite the short-term risks to the stock, analysts said that Nvidia is still solidly positioned to be an AI chip leader for the long term. "Can it be managed forward? That's the real question. I think it can, because Jensen has instilled, has set the company up to succeed. He set the pace, set the tone, and established such deep, entrenched relationships and agreements within the industry that if he left, I don't think anything would change at Nvidia for at least the next couple years," said Cody Acree, an analyst at StoneX. Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson said there may not be any substantive long-term effect on the company provided there's a solid transition plan in place for Huang. "If he has to leave … if there's good succession and an orderly transition, I don't think there's going to be any impact to the company," he said. Nvidia said Colette Kress would be interim CEO. She has been the CFO since 2013. – Paulina Likos contributed reporting More In Pro Analysis
